title: CS QBR SLI Workshop Notes — latency, uptime, cost-per-token, cache-hit
body:
Purpose:
This is a working workshop capture: definitions, measurement recipes, and simple KPI tables we can drop into QBR decks and the renewal tracker. Goal is to produce one canonical SLI spec per customer tier (self-serve, mid-market, enterprise) + a short playbook for alerts/remediation.

Context / why: 
- Customers keep asking for consistent ways we measure latency and uptime in health reviews. CS needs reproducible rules so QBRs don't diverge between AEs.
- Engineering has asked for concise SLO recipes they can implement and instrument in telemetry.
- We want renewal signals mapped to metric drift bands (low/medium/high risk).

Quick summary recommendations (workshop outputs):
1) Latency: 7-day rolling P95 for interactive endpoints, 95th for generation-heavy customers; use client-observed end-to-end where possible.
2) Uptime: monthly availability calculated as 1 - (sum_downtime_seconds / seconds_in_month) for customer-facing endpoints; report % with two decimal places.
3) Cost-per-token: measure using billed tokens / user-facing tokens over a 30-day window; include tokenization assumptions in notes.
4) Cache hit rate: prefix+KV hit rate measured at the request-router layer; report both absolute hit% and effective saved-tokens estimate.

Metric definitions (text-first canonical forms):
- Latency (Interactive P95): definition: 95th percentile of end-to-end request latency (client request timestamp -> final byte sent) computed over a 7-day sliding window. Aggregation: per-route, per-model. Units: milliseconds. Target: <= 350ms for self-serve, <= 200ms for enterprise dedicated routes. Measurement caveats: exclude synthetic/healthcheck requests; include retries as separate requests.

- Latency (Generation P95): definition: 95th percentile of time-to-final-token for streaming generation endpoints. Window: 7-day. Units: ms per request. Target: depends on model+seq; include expected seq length in QBR notes.

- Uptime (monthly availability): definition: Availability = 1 - (total_incident_downtime_seconds / seconds_in_month) for all customer-facing endpoints mapped to the account. Window: calendar month. Target: 99.9% for enterprise contracts, 99.5% for standard. Notes: scheduled maintenance announced in advance does not count as downtime if opted into maintenance window.

- Cost-per-token (effective billed): definition: Total billed cost from billing export / total user-facing tokens (inbound+outbound as defined by tokenizer rules) over a 30-day rolling window. Units: USD/token with 6 decimal places. Important: normalize for quantization (e.g., if customer uses quantized model variants, note the model family in the QBR row).

- Cache Hit Rate (prefix + KV combined): definition: hits / (hits + misses) measured at the routing layer for matchable requests. Report both: (a) raw hit%, (b) effective tokens saved = sum_tokens_avoided_by_hit / sum_tokens_total. Window: 14-day to catch weekly patterns. Notes: include separate counts for warm-cache vs cold-cache (first N minutes after deployment).

Sample KPI table (copyable into QBR slide):
Metric | Definition (short) | Window | Aggregate | Target | Current | Owner | Notes
--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Latency (P95 interactive) | End-to-end P95 (ms) | 7-day | per-route, per-model | <=350ms | 420ms | eng-observability | High tail due to batching on route / discuss batching override
Uptime (availability) | 1 - downtime/s_month (%) | 30-day | account-level | 99.5% | 99.92% | sre | include recent incident IDs in appendix
Cost-per-token | billed $ / tokens | 30-day | account-level | $0.0008 | $0.0012 | finance-integrations | includes quantized inference adjustments
Cache hit rate | hits/(hits+misses) (%) | 14-day | route-level | >=45% | 32% | eng-serving | see cache-warmup note; KV misses spike on rollout

Sample numerical interpretation examples (for CS):
- If P95 latency > target by 20% for two consecutive weeks -> classify as "Performance degradation" flag. Trigger: open support ticket and schedule engineer-led public post-mortem with CS/AE.
- If cost-per-token increases >30% vs baseline and renewal within 90 days -> flag as "Econ risk" and propose Redwood Optimize audit.
- Cache hit rate < target and cache-savings < 10% of token spend -> propose caching tuning + prefetch rules in solutions engineering workshop.

Alert & remedial playbook (short):
Trigger -> Immediate action -> Escalation timeline -> Owner
P95 drift (>20% over baseline) -> Collect traces, notify on-call, replicate with synthetic workload -> 2 business days -> eng-sre + AE
Uptime drop below SLA -> Page SRE, notify customer success and account owner, create incident bridge -> immediate -> SRE/infra -> weekly status to customer
Cost spike (>30% month-over-month) -> Pull billing export, rerun tokenization sample, check model variants, propose throttle/quantization switch -> 1 week -> customer-success + finance + solutions-eng
Cache hit regression (drop >10pt) -> Check recent deploys, identify keys with high churn, roll back change or apply rule-based TTL increase -> 3 business days -> eng-serving + solutions-eng

Measurement recipes (what telemetry to surface):
- Latency: prefer client-observed headers when available (client-sent timestamp) and fall back to edge-timing. Capture percentiles and counts for request size buckets.
- Uptime: incident log with start/end timestamps; attribute to customer endpoints via routing metadata.
- Cost-per-token: join billing CSV (cost) with telemetry token counts using request IDs. Provide sample SQL snippet in Confluence.
- Cache: router-level counters exposed to metrics backend, plus a daily sample of hits/misses with representative request IDs for debugging.

Open questions (to resolve before canonicalization):
- Do we standardize on P95 (interactive) and P95 or P99 (generation) for all customers, or continue per-account ops? (action: product + eng to propose by 2025-02-15)
- How to treat blended endpoints used by multiple customers behind the same route? Need mapping logic. (action: eng-observability to propose mapping rules)
- Tokenization normalization: which tokenizer version do we lock for 30-day cost comparisons? (action: finance + research)

Appendix: quick formulas and example SQL snippets (paste-ready):
- availability_pct = 1 - (sum(downtime_seconds) / 2592000.0) -- 30 day approx
- p95_latency = quantile(0.95, latency_ms) over 7d
- cost_per_token = sum(billed_usd) / sum(tokens_count) over 30d

Action items from workshop: 
- [A1] Product to finalize latency percentile policy (P95 vs P99) for generation workloads — owner: Priya Nambiar, due 2025-02-15.
- [A2] SRE to publish mapping doc for shared-route attribution — owner: Aaron Lee, due 2025-02-22.
- [A3] CS to add the KPI table template to renewal tracker as a new tab and wire sample formulas — owner: Sofia Martinez, due 2025-02-07.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc short; move heavy SQL and long examples to Confluence link above.
- We should produce two variants of the KPI slide: "customer-facing" (one metric row each) and "engineer-facing" (per-route breakdown).

References and prior docs mentioned:

- Existing tracker: renewal-tracker-v4 (spreadsheet)
- Slack thread: #cs-qbr -> timestamped discussions (linked in metadata)

End of workshop capture.
